title: Bitwise Operations
description:
## Bitwise Operations
Bitwise operations work on individual bits. Essential for low-level programming.

- `and rax, rbx` - bits are 1 only if BOTH are 1
- `or rax, rbx` - bits are 1 if EITHER is 1
- `xor rax, rbx` - bits are 1 if they're DIFFERENT
- `not rax` - flips all bits
- `shl rax, n` - shift bits left by n (multiply by 2^n)
- `shr rax, n` - shift bits right by n (divide by 2^n)

```
and: 1010 & 1100 = 1000
or:  1010 | 1100 = 1110
xor: 1010 ^ 1100 = 0110
not: ~1010       = 0101
```

You already know one trick: `xor rdi, rdi` sets `rdi` to 0. Now you know why - anything XOR itself is always 0.
